newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Two Bahraini plot suspects jailed.
newsitem.headline: Two Bahraini plot suspects jailed.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Wednesday sentenced two men accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iran plot to topple the government to 15 and 12 years in jail, sources close to the court said.
They said Ali al-Muqawi was sentenced to 15 years and Sheikh Jassim al-Kayat to 12 years.

The trial of 81 suspects -- 22 of them in absentia -- began on March 1. They were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Lawyers had said they could have faced the death penalty.
The verdicts were announced on the first anniversary of the execution by firing squad of Ahmed Hassan Qamber for killing a policeman.
Bahrain last June accused Iran of an attempt to topple the island's government by force. Iran denied the charge.
Sentencing of others on trial was continuing.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the largely Sunni government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
